channel.title: Vedang Vatsa | Essays
channel.description: Essays on AI, technology, and the future by Vedang Vatsa.

item.title: Who Buys After the Layoff
item.description: AI can cut a wage without cutting a customer, change a job, or create a new one. The open question is which of those three happens to the receipt.

item.title: When Agents Stop Speaking English
item.description: A2A's sample message is still Hello, world. MCP and A2A already send JSON. Tickets and payments already use fields. The English in the sample is leftover from chat.

item.title: The IndiaAI Mission
item.description: India approved ₹10,372 crore for an AI mission. By 9 February 2026, ₹401 crore had arrived. Officials count onboarded GPUs. Parliament later published hours sanctioned, not hours used.

item.title: The Neocloud
item.description: CoreWeave calls itself a giant cloud company. Its IPO filing showed Microsoft as 62% of 2024 sales. The March 2026 loan was rated on the GPU rack and the customer contract. That is a renter with a pay-anyway lease, not AWS.

item.title: A Mind That Outlives You
item.description: OpenAI built ChatGPT memory for multi-year time horizons. Apple, Google, and Facebook already have dead-user tools. The assistants that now hold the running notes of a life still do not.

item.title: Private Cognition
item.description: You can encrypt a disk. You cannot yet encrypt a thought at ChatGPT prices. Apple's Private Cloud Compute is a shipped TEE. Zama's FHE still clocks a GPT-2 token in seconds. Zero data retention is a contract. Coverage uses one word for all three.

item.title: Does Half the Web Run on Bots?
item.description: The web pays for itself when a bot visits and a person follows. AI crawlers now copy the page, answer elsewhere, and leave the site with the hosting bill.

item.title: Open-Weight Licences
item.description: Labs call the weights open. The files are Apache, MIT, Community, or Research. You can run the download. You cannot check the training data. Llama still has a veto at 700 million users.

item.title: The National AI Compute Scorecard
item.description: 6 countries took different approaches to national AI compute. Each programme counts a different thing.

item.title: Sovereign AI Debt
item.description: Stargate was announced as $500 billion. By August 2025 Bloomberg reported that funds had not been raised to that budget. MGX later closed a $40 billion acquisition. SoftBank borrowed to buy OpenAI shares. Announced, funded, and spent still get printed as one investment number.

item.title: AI Safety Institutes
item.description: Every capital launched a safety institute. The UK hired. The US renamed the shop and kept about $15 million in public cash. The EU built an Office that can fine. The word spread. The statute did not.

item.title: The AI Lawsuit Ledger
item.description: Two hundred AI suits sit on public dockets. One produced a $1.5 billion cheque. The Times has spent $28 million and does not have a verdict. The paid column is almost entirely people who did not sue.

item.title: Intelligence is a Commodity
item.description: You can now buy intelligence at a monthly price. Higher list prices buy longer reasoning. Access is cheaper. Expertise is not the same as a list price.

item.title: Building an AI Text Detector
item.description: Data, stylometric features, and production limits for AI text detection at scale.

item.title: The State of AI
item.description: An OpenAlex sweep of 5,003,783 papers whose abstracts match AI method terms, 2013 through mid-2026. Neural networks still lead the cumulative count. LLM mentions grew 29.9x from 2018 to 2025. China leads volume. The US still leads LLM papers. 48.9% of the corpus has zero citations.

item.title: The State of Web3
item.description: On 12 June 2026 OpenAlex tagged 128,286 blockchain papers. Yearly output grew 117 times from 2013 to 2025. A paper total is not a count of working software or of statutes in force.

item.title: The Agent Infrastructure Stack
item.description: Over $5 billion in venture capital has been deployed into the eight layers of infrastructure that AI agents need to function.

item.title: The Great Funding Realignment
item.description: An empirical study of global venture capital cycles from 2015 to 2026, analyzing capital concentration, the expansion of median check sizes, and the Seed-to-Series A transition bottleneck.

item.title: The AI Implementation Playbook
item.description: A complete, step-by-step framework for implementing AI agents across every function of a startup. From brand consistency to automated outreach to SEO that runs itself.

item.title: The Post-Interface Internet
item.description: The GUI was a 40-year hack for human-computer impedance matching.

item.title: Agents Eating SaaS
item.description: The $400 billion SaaS industry was built on per-seat pricing. AI agents do not sit in seats.

item.title: The Agentic State
item.description: Estonia claims 100% of government services are online. Singapore deployed AI across its public service at scale.

item.title: The Text Field is the New Dashboard
item.description: When a text field backed by an LLM can answer any question by calling internal APIs directly, the dashboard becomes redundant.

item.title: The Stepwise Approach to Enterprise AI
item.description: Most enterprises fail at AI by deploying it everywhere at once. Evidence shows that starting with narrow, high-frequency tasks produces measurable ROI.

item.title: Post-Scarcity Technology
item.description: When the marginal cost of intelligence, energy, and digital goods trends toward zero, the economic frameworks built on scarcity face structural pressure.

item.title: Agentic Commerce
item.description: When algorithms start shopping on behalf of consumers, traditional e-commerce breaks.

item.title: Towards the Agentic Web
item.description: How the internet is shifting from a place where humans find information to a platform where autonomous AI agents get things done on your behalf.

item.title: The Infinity Economy
item.description: Can AI and decentralized systems make scarcity obsolete, or does the physical world have something to say about that?

item.title: The AI Economy

item.description: How a fishing village became one of the richest countries on earth, and what the development economics literature says about why.

item.title: From Cheap to Competitive
item.description: How national product quality perception follows income growth with a predictable lag, and where India sits on that arc today.

item.description: Vendor reports put deepfake volume up hundreds of percent. Human detection of high-quality fakes is near chance in lab work. Official loss tallies lag.

item.title: Governance for AGI
item.description: Three regulatory superpowers are building incompatible AI governance frameworks. The EU bans practices. The US deregulates. China registers algorithms.

item.title: The Substrate Shift
item.description: Silicon is hitting physical limits at the atomic scale. DNA stores 455 exabytes per gram.

item.title: The World as an Interface
item.description: The smart home market will reach $175 billion in 2025. Device shipments approach 1.25 billion units.

item.title: What is the Singularity?
item.description: The word, the alignment problem, and why the only speed question that matters is a week versus a decade. Dates live elsewhere.

item.title: API States
item.description: Estonia runs 99% of public services digitally and saves 2% of GDP annually. India's UPI processes billions of transactions monthly.

item.description: The average attention span on a screen is 47 seconds. A 2025 US survey put daily phone checks at 205.

item.title: Digital Monasticism
item.description: Silence is the new luxury. The average person spends 7 hours on screens daily. Gloria Mark's mean screen attention is 47 seconds. The median is 40.

item.title: Attention Refinery
item.description: The five largest technology companies generate over $600 billion per year by extracting and reselling human attention.

item.description: An analysis of blockchain's evolution from cryptographic experiment to institutional infrastructure, examining what survived the hype cycles, where the...

item.title: Sacred Algorithms
item.description: COMPAS predicts recidivism with racial bias baked in. Healthcare AI underestimates illness in minority patients.

item.title: Computational Social Science
item.description: Twitter's API shutdown disrupted 20 years of social research. Digital twins simulate voter behavior.

item.title: Computational Constitutions
item.description: Wyoming legalized DAO LLCs in 2021. Smart contracts execute governance rules automatically.

item.title: Pseudonymous Agency
item.description: Satoshi Nakamoto built a $1 trillion protocol without revealing an identity. Banksy generates $25M+ per auction without a face.

item.title: Programmable Trust
item.description: Zero-knowledge proofs verify without revealing. Trusted execution environments create hardware-enforced privacy.

item.title: The God Protocol
item.description: Nick Szabo imagined a trusted third party with infinite integrity, no self-interest, and perfect confidentiality. Bitcoin approximated it.

item.title: The Sensory Internet
item.description: The haptic technology market reaches $4-12 billion in 2025. Apple shipped 390,000 Vision Pro units. Neuralink implanted its first human BCI.

item.title: The Mesh Economy
item.description: DeFi protocols execute billions in daily volume with zero employees. DAOs manage tens of billions in treasury assets through on-chain governance.

item.title: The Plurality Trap
item.description: More information was supposed to produce better understanding. Instead, it produced more ways to be wrong confidently.

item.title: The Simulation Layer
item.description: Digital twins save Boeing over $1 billion in manufacturing. Waymo has driven 20+ billion simulated miles.
